classification.evidence: eight relations over nine boxes whose content is identifiers and qualifiers, not phases: eno16595np0, 25GbE, 103.19.91.58/29, .57/.59/.60-.62, AS132717, AS13335, 14.143.x/14.141.x, plus measured hop latencies 0.1/1.8/7.1/8.6 ms and qualified states (7 ports dark, 'free?', OUI-derived vendor, 'no probe reply'). E = N, so omission is the only real failure mode.
tie_breakers_considered: density: E (8) = N (9) - no edge surplus, so not a mesh and not a fabric
anti-parallel pair: none in the source (every relation is a one-way observation: uplink, membership, transit hop) - not a service-mesh
bus with disconnected worlds: the /29 members are not a bus - three separate membership facts, and the source names no shared corridor; a trunk would bundle independent facts - not placement-planes
motion: the source is a static traceroute/addressing snapshot, never animates anything - not a lifecycle machine, and dots are forbidden by the 'static source' rule
identifier/qualifier content outranks shape: the hard part is that every address, AS number, device name and uncertainty marker survives, so identity-probe-maps
classification.secondary_recipe_applied: none. The ToR does receive a fan of three edges, which is the service-mesh signature, but those edges are independent membership observations with no anti-parallel pair and no request/response semantics, so the mesh recipe does not apply. The egress half of the case is a plain chain (gw -> airtel -> airtelbb -> cf) and follows the identity-map chain treatment.
classification.reclassification_during_work: none. The family was fixed before the first spec and never changed.
